text:
sam: heads up — after the kernel-selector roll (v2.1.3) we see a small but steady host-side overhead bump on ingress paths. p50 up ~2ms, p99 up ~18ms, CPU on proxy hosts +12%.
ciara-bot: alert triggered: host_ingress_cpu spike on pool-hosts (avg 12% above baseline) — rule: host-ingress-cpu-5m
li: reproduce steps? saw similar on staging earlier but blamed quantization path. this sounds different.
sam: repro is pretty deterministic on the canary: 5k qps synthetic with short prompts (avg tokens/request 18). run ./bench/mini-ingress --qps 5k --seq 18 --conns 200.
marco: attaching a tiny log excerpt from the canary (trimmed):
```
[ingress] recv 200 conns
[parse] frames=512 writev_calls=1487 avg_frag=340B
[tokenize] batches=5200 kv_lookup_ms_avg=0.6
[stream] chunk_coalesce_ms_avg=1.8
```
sam: notable: writev calls per second jumped ~20% vs previous deploy. also allocs/sec +8% in host proxy.
anya: could be the new kernel selection causing slightly different fragment sizes that prevent coalesce. also maybe the preparse path now does an extra memcpy for small frames.
marco: I ran a short eBPF trace — here's the hot stack (symbols simplified):
```
writev
nghttp2_submit_data
ingress_preparse::serialize_frame
tokenizer::split
memcpy
```
li: interesting — memcpy shows up. can we try flipping kernel selector back to older policy on the canary and compare?
sam: already scheduled. action: 1) flip selector to legacy-fast on canary, 2) run bench, 3) capture writev/allocs. marco/anya to own traces.
marco: I'll run the flip and bench in ~30m and post numbers.
anya: I'll add lightweight jemalloc counters and an extra tracepoint around preparse memcpy.
li: if flipping fixes it, next step is to look at kernel decision heuristics — maybe a threshold misclassification for short sequences. we should also check kv cache hot miss pattern; small fragments hurt coalesce + kv lookup + writev.
sam: noted. priority high but not paging SRE yet. rolling rollback if canary regressions hit >15% p99 increase.
ciara-bot: deployment event: rolled back selector -> legacy-fast on canary at 1760000060 by marco
marco: quick numbers after flip (first 5m): p50 restored, p99 reduced from +18ms to +4ms, writev calls down ~17%, host CPU back within 1% of baseline.
li: great signal. next: instrument the selector code path for fragment-size histogram and add test harness to generate short-frag heavy traffic.
sam: thanks — create a tiny RFC PR with proposed fixes for kernel selector heuristics + unit tests and link it here. we'll track until next deploy. :thumbsup:
